mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen 3.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w (-51.4 to -48.3), signaling an unbroken upward trend. This momentum persists over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the baseline mean of the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.4 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below -48.3 or declines week-on-week in three of four weeks ahead.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered from -49.6 to -45.6 (4.0 point gain), indicating commuter return. When TRANSIT rises above -46, office workers resume weekday routines, increasing incidental retail visits and lifting RETAIL_REC above its current level within two weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -47 in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed -48.3 by week t+2.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near -19 (from -25.1 at t-3w), while RESIDENTIAL has declined from 13.0 to 11.1. This shift indicates outdoor recreation substitution for home confinement. Sustained park usage signals consumer confidence, which spills into retail spending over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above -20 AND RESIDENTIAL below 12
failure_condition: PARKS falls below -25 or RESIDENTIAL rises above 13 in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines from -48.3.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has improved from -22.4 to -18.6 (3.8 point gain), indicating relaxed restrictions on essential retail. When essential retail access improves, policy constraints on discretionary retail ease simultaneously, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20 in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not improve by week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has remained flat at -46.7 (variance < 1 point across four weeks), indicating no workplace return. Persistent workplace absence suppresses retail footfall from commuters and lunch-hour shoppers, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below -48 over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stable at -46.7 across all four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -45 in any week ahead, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -47 as a four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined steadily from 13.0 to 11.1 over four weeks. Continued decline signals spring/early summer outdoor migration away from home. This behavioral shift reduces retail-and-recreation demand as consumers substitute outdoor activities for indoor shopping, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.9 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 12 in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC improves by more than 2 percentage points from -48.3.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show divergent signals: TRANSIT recovered 4.0 points while WORKPLACES stalled. This decoupling indicates transit use for non-work purposes (leisure, shopping). When TRANSIT improves without WORKPLACES recovery, retail footfall rises from discretionary mobility, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises > 3 points week-on-week AND WORKPLACES remains flat (±1 point)
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES converge (both rise or both fall by >2 points), or RETAIL_REC does not exceed -48 by week t+2.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM have both improved (6.2 and 3.8 points respectively), signaling consumer confidence in outdoor and essential activities. This dual confidence signal predicts retail-and-recreation recovery: consumers willing to visit parks and stores will increase discretionary retail visits within one week.
failure_condition: Either PARKS or GROCERY_PHARM falls below their t-0w levels in the next week, or RETAIL_REC does not improve by week t+1.
